title: Week 5 Mastery Quiz · Regimes, Democracy, and Authoritarianism

questions.question: Simulated election record: Party A wins 54% of votes but 82% of seats under district plurality rules. What can be concluded?
options: The system translated votes into a disproportionate seat share; fairness needs further institutional analysis
The disproportionate seat share independently establishes ballot-count manipulation.
Because Party A gained more than half the votes, it is entitled to every seat.
District-level plurality counts require no further evidence about geographic vote distribution.
questions.explanation: The system translated votes into a disproportionate seat share; fairness needs further institutional analysis

questions.question: A fictional state holds regular elections but bans independent opposition newspapers. Which additional regime dimension is most directly at issue?
options: National population
Civil liberties and meaningful political competition
Whether the constitution has a preamble
The number of official holidays
questions.explanation: Civil liberties and meaningful political competition

questions.question: Document A reports 80% turnout; Document B documents opposition candidate exclusions. What is the defensible synthesis?
options: Turnout proves a liberal democracy
Excluded candidates prove that nobody voted
Participation and competition measure distinct conditions; evaluate both
No comparison is possible
questions.explanation: Participation and competition measure distinct conditions; evaluate both

questions.question: Simulated 12-year institutional timeline: elected officials increasingly ignore adverse court decisions. Which trend does this best suggest?
options: Growth in judicial independence
A guaranteed coup
Proof of constitutional amendment
Potential erosion of checks and accountability requiring corroboration
questions.explanation: Potential erosion of checks and accountability requiring corroboration

questions.question: A state constitution guarantees assembly rights, while verified municipal ordinances prohibit peaceful gatherings. What question comes first?
options: Whether legal guarantees are meaningfully implemented and enforceable
Whether the flag has changed
How many parties use the word freedom
Whether assembly rights appear in a textbook
questions.explanation: Whether legal guarantees are meaningfully implemented and enforceable

questions.question: Two authoritarian systems differ: one is dominated by a military council and another by a single family. Which evidence distinguishes the mechanisms?
options: Climate data
Decision-making appointments, coercive organizations, and succession records
Only voting age
The national anthem
questions.explanation: Decision-making appointments, coercive organizations, and succession records

questions.question: An election-monitoring report covers only urban polling sites. Which limitation matters for a national fairness claim?
options: There are no relevant limitations
Urban results must match rural ones
Geographic coverage may miss rural irregularities or distinct conditions
Observers always know every outcome
questions.explanation: Geographic coverage may miss rural irregularities or distinct conditions

questions.question: Fictional policy record: the election commission is legally independent but its budget is controlled by the incumbent cabinet. What must an analyst investigate?
options: Only its official name
Whether its offices have security guards
The number of ballot colors
Whether financial control affects operational autonomy and enforcement
questions.explanation: Whether financial control affects operational autonomy and enforcement

questions.question: A historian compares a 1990 decree and 2020 election law but omits interim amendments. What is the strongest correction?
options: Reconstruct the legal chronology before asserting continuity or change
Treat the newer law as unchanged by definition
Use slogans to fill the gap
Remove all dates
questions.explanation: Reconstruct the legal chronology before asserting continuity or change

questions.question: A government cites high economic growth as proof that its elections are competitive. Which analytical correction is appropriate?
options: Growth proves electoral integrity
Economic performance and political competition require separate evidence
Competitive elections always lower growth
One indicator measures all regime dimensions
questions.explanation: Economic performance and political competition require separate evidence

shortResponse: Which institutional evidence distinguishes democracy, hybrid regimes, and authoritarian rule?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
